title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented JMU rituals, legends, and recurring practices, from game-day streamers to the university’s oldest alumni tradition.

cards.title: Wear Purple on Friday
cards.subtitle: JMU’s weekly show-your-colors ritual
cards.notes: Put on purple before Friday classes and join the recurring campus-wide display of JMU colors documented by the university.
cards.short_summary: Friday turns JMU’s primary color into a wearable weekly ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s official spirit-and-traditions page says that members of the campus community wear purple especially on Fridays.
cards.access_notes: A campus custom rather than a scheduled or restricted event.

cards.title: Answer “J-M-U” with “Duuuuukes”
cards.subtitle: The shouted response comes with its own arm sweep
cards.notes: When you hear “J-M-U,” reply “Duuuuukes,” step forward, and sweep both arms outward as the official tradition guide describes.
cards.short_summary: A three-letter shout triggers a word, a step, and a synchronized gesture.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU instructs fans to answer a shout of “J-M-U” with “Duuuuukes” while stepping forward and sweeping their arms outward.
cards.access_notes: Typically practiced in school-spirit and game-day settings; follow the rules of the event venue.

cards.title: Throw Purple and Gold After a Touchdown
cards.subtitle: Bridgeforth celebrations arrive as airborne streamers
cards.notes: Bring only venue-permitted purple or gold streamers, then throw them after a JMU football touchdown and clean up responsibly.
cards.short_summary: JMU touchdowns cue a burst of purple-and-gold paper above the crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s official traditions guide directs fans to throw purple or gold streamers when the football team scores a touchdown.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires entry to a football game; consult current stadium policies before carrying streamers inside.

cards.title: Shout the Fight Song with the MRDs
cards.subtitle: A former Madisonians show tune became the game-day anthem
cards.notes: Learn the official words before game day, then join in when the Marching Royal Dukes take the field instead of guessing through the chorus.
cards.short_summary: The marching band’s entrance cues a song adapted from an older campus show tune.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU identifies shouting the Fight Song when the Marching Royal Dukes take the field as a game-day practice; Athletics says George West adapted it from “We Are the Madisonians.”
cards.access_notes: The official Athletics page provides the words and an audio download; live participation depends on event admission.

cards.title: Hold the Door for the Next Duke
cards.subtitle: A tiny courtesy promoted as a JMU way of life
cards.notes: Pause at campus doors and hold one for the person behind you; keep pathways clear and respect anyone who prefers more space.
cards.short_summary: At JMU, an everyday doorway courtesy is treated as a campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s official traditions page describes holding doors open for others as a characteristic campus practice centered on care and kindness.
cards.access_notes: Practice the courtesy only at buildings and spaces where you are otherwise authorized to enter.

cards.title: Add a Layer to Spirit Rock
cards.subtitle: Years of campus messages are stacked in paint
cards.notes: Photograph the current message or join an authorized painting activity; use the rock as intended and leave nearby surfaces untouched.
cards.short_summary: A campus boulder serves as JMU’s continually repainted public canvas.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU says the Madison Society installed Spirit Rock as a canvas for campus artists and that years of expression have covered it in layers of paint.
cards.access_notes: Painting procedures are not stated on the cited page; confirm current campus authorization before adding paint.

cards.title: Walk Around the Quad Seal
cards.subtitle: Students avoid one engraved landmark on the way to Wilson Hall
cards.notes: Look down on the Wilson Hall approach, photograph the Alma Mater inscription, and follow the documented custom by walking around the seal.
cards.short_summary: Respect for the Alma Mater is expressed by taking a small detour.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU tells visitors not to step on the Quad seal and says students walk around it as a sign of love and respect for their Alma Mater.
cards.access_notes: The seal is embedded in the outdoor walkway leading toward Wilson Hall; remain attentive to pedestrian traffic.

cards.title: Test the Kissing Rock Legend
cards.subtitle: A leftover limestone outcrop acquired a marriage prediction
cards.notes: Visit the limestone landmark with a consenting partner, take a photo, and treat its marriage prediction as campus folklore—not a promise.
cards.short_summary: An immovable construction obstacle became the setting for JMU’s romantic legend.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s history says couples used the rock for private goodnight kisses in the 1920s and that the legend later predicted those who kissed there would marry.
cards.access_notes: The rock is on the Quad near Alumnae Hall; participation is optional and always requires mutual consent.

cards.title: Pass the Flame into Alumni Life
cards.subtitle: JMU’s oldest Madison Tradition closes senior year
cards.notes: As graduation nears, check the Alumni Association schedule and register for the candle-lighting and pinning ceremony on the Quad.
cards.short_summary: Graduating Dukes mark their transition through shared candlelight and an alumni pin.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU calls Senior Candle Lighting its oldest Madison Tradition and says graduating seniors are inducted into the Alumni Association through candle lighting and pinning.
cards.access_notes: The cited 2026 ceremony was for the Class of 2026; future seniors should confirm the current date, eligibility, registration, and fee.

cards.title: Take the First-Day Photo on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Wilson Hall anchors JMU’s annual back-to-class portrait
cards.notes: Stop at the Quad photo setup on the first day of fall classes, pose with Wilson Hall behind you, and download the published image later.
cards.short_summary: The first day of classes comes with an official Wilson Hall portrait.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU says it offers students a first-day-of-classes photo opportunity every fall and lists archived photo collections dating back to 2017.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 event was scheduled outdoors on the Quad; verify the current year’s date, time, and weather arrangements.
